recommendation.rationale: A precisely documented boundary between file-format validity and reproducible quantitative measurement, accessible real CC BY image/label pairs, feasible small executable realization, and directly relevant published human-service rates. This supports a useful prototype study, not a demonstrated new market or unearned algorithmic novelty.
recommendation.caveat: Strong existing viewers, format validators, feature extractors and specialist workflows must be present in E. The study may establish successful delivery and actual artifact transfer while E+ versus E remains zero. Count/volume preservation must not be equated with correct biological segmentation.
recommendation.decisive_first_step: Acquire one actual public labeled image subset, record byte provenance/license, calculate source-space object statistics using existing tools, then prospectively freeze a transfer contract before applying two representation changes and testing a separate recipient.
recommendation.selected_by_root: Quantitative microscopy: preserve count/native physical volume/mapped geometric volume/centroid using source-segmentation affine moment transport; old analytical formulas remain competent baseline.
recommendation.novelty_scope: Constructed usable measurement capability and inspected conditional service arrangement, not novel affine mathematics.

candidates.title: Quantitative microscopy measurement continuity across image pipelines
candidates.beneficiary: Research laboratories and imaging core facilities that must reuse expensive image acquisitions and segmentations in another viewer, analysis pipeline or collaborator environment.
candidates.outcome: A reproducible export/analysis package demonstrating that requested cell/object counts, physical volumes or centroids retain their stated meaning; unsupported transformations produce a specific observation/requalification request.
candidates.existing: OME-Zarr/NGFF stores scalable images, labels and physical coordinate transforms. ome-zarr-models already converts metadata between 0.5 and 0.6. ngff-zarr implements transformations/resampling. OME provides validators, conformance tests and an interoperability matrix. Nyxus and many conventional tools already extract features.
candidates.gap: NGFF v0.6 explicitly excludes exact transformed/resampled pixel reproducibility. A syntactically valid dataset can leave the quantitative mission unqualified because of interpolation, coordinate-system identity, axis/units, pixel extent, missing metadata or version-specific reader behavior. The unproven narrow service opportunity is a mission-specific measurement continuity package, not conversion or segmentation itself.
candidates.why_now: Recent v0.6 coordinate-system support provides explicit transformation structures that a small instrument can inspect; frontier agents can construct/test adapters, but no measured frontier advantage is established by this search.
candidates.construction: Use existing readers and transforms. Bind original measurements, coordinate frame, label semantics, accepted numerical tolerances and downstream purpose. Execute before/after measurements and output machine-readable evidence and human-readable inspection. Retain the compiler/measurement contract tool with version, dependencies and provenance.
candidates.first_test: One publicly licensed real image+label pair. Predefine count/volume/centroid tolerances. Test one representation change that should preserve measures, one lossy resampling that may not, and a missing/contradictory transform that requires hold. Expert baseline gets the same docs, tools and data. Freeze before a second image/recipient task.
candidates.falsifier: If standard tooling with a concise script delivers identical accepted output at equal or lower complete costs, there is no E+ advantage/newly feasible service; retain only the useful artifact and delivery result. If source segmentation lacks ground truth, refrain from biological validity claims.
candidates.arrangement: Possible imaging-core fee-for-service or shared adapter construction among laboratories with compatible actual needs. Compare individual setup versus shared fixed construction plus lab-specific verification. Model nonparticipation, incompatible microscopy workflows, rights, support, delivery failure, withdrawals, refunds and prefunding. No lab interest observed.
candidates.human_reference: CHUM lists formatted image-analysis delivery at $129.75/h for external academic/hospital clients and $143.50/h for businesses. Scope is broad analysis, not exact proposed audit. Team hours and direct equivalence require assumptions/measurement. Page uses $ without explicit currency statement in extracted text; CAD is geographically plausible but must remain disclosed if unverified.
candidates.data: IDR catalog contains CC BY 4.0 image+label pairs 6001240.zarr (idr0062, 271x275x236, two channels) and 5514375.zarr (idr0052, 256x256x31, three channels, forty times), and coordinate-translation cases 13457537/13457539. Retrieve a bounded ROI/label volume with exact hashes. Samples are not yet acquired.

candidates.title: Accessible transit contingency construction under incomplete outage information
candidates.beneficiary: Wheelchair passengers, accessibility coordinators and transit operators.
candidates.outcome: An inspectable itinerary with actual end-to-end physical accessibility evidence, contingency routes and explicit checks still required before relying on it.
candidates.existing: GTFS Pathways represents station geometry and travel modes. OpenTripPlanner supports wheelchair route restrictions, slope limits, accessible transfers and explicit costs or refusal for unknown accessibility. Agency feeds and existing MTA MCP tools expose outages and alternate-route information.
candidates.gap: GTFS documentation itself describes equipment-failure/outage reporting as an extension need. The remaining unproven gap is assembling a purpose-preserving contingency and a targeted information-acquisition plan when observations are stale or missing. Generic route planning/outage display is already supplied.
candidates.why_now: Public pathway schemas and agency feeds plus model tool-use could support cross-feed interpretation. No evidence yet that agents outperform competent accessibility staff or tools.
candidates.construction: A graph compiler distinguishing known accessible, known inaccessible and unknown links; bind freshness and observation source; compute contingencies under declared outage scenarios and identify minimal unresolved information. Never treat penalties as proof of accessibility.
candidates.first_test: Official GTFS Waterfront-station example and another station with public pathway fixtures; test outage and unknown-state cases. Expert baseline receives same graph and direct graph algorithms. Label actual outage status unavailable/simulated; do not provide real passenger operational advice.
candidates.falsifier: Existing OTP configuration plus standard closure enumeration yields equal contingency quality/cost, or required physical access data is absent. Then no new capability claim; publish missing-information diagnosis only.
candidates.arrangement: Operator-sponsored accessibility data/contingency maintenance; possible shared pathway surveying among venues. Willingness to pay unknown, safety obligations and live-feed reliability matter.
candidates.data: GTFS official example contains explicit stops/pathways rows; MBTA official API and docs provide current service/alert interfaces. Real pilot cannot assume optional fields are complete.

candidates.title: Discriminating water-system faults from physical events by targeted added observation
candidates.beneficiary: Water utility operations and research teams facing unreliable sensors and ambiguous alarms.
candidates.outcome: A bounded diagnostic that identifies which event classes remain observationally indistinguishable and proposes an extra measurement capable of separating them.
candidates.existing: EPA/Sandia WNTR supports hydraulics/quality/resilience simulations; SPOT already optimizes sensor placement. Existing research formulates minimum test cover, observability, uncertainty-aware sampling and fault-aware contamination prioritization. A June 2026 paper addresses sensor faults and contamination jointly.
candidates.gap: Potential narrow opportunity is identifying specific ambiguity for a particular buyer task and economical targeted confirmation. Generic detection, sensor optimization or autoencoder fault reconstruction is not novel.
candidates.why_now: A small real testbed dataset and transparent simulators are available. They could support an executable refusal/observation instrument but not substantiate production reliability.
candidates.construction: Compare latent event hypotheses against observable channels; expose equivalence sets and extra sensor/measurement requirements; test retained hypothesis-elimination instrument on a new network/mission.
candidates.first_test: WDSEventDB's small 2.3 MB testbed dataset (leakage, attacks, sensor failure), if licensing and bytes are acquired, plus declared simulated perturbations. Compare conventional multivariate residual and explicit hypothesis enumeration baselines.
candidates.falsifier: The proposed extra observation does not separate the hypotheses under uncertainty, or expert standard tooling achieves the same result. Existing diagnosis research strongly challenges novelty.
candidates.arrangement: Contracted diagnostic assessment/recalibration support, with prospective real pilot before any safety or production claims. No actual demand, field validation or authorized utility connection.
candidates.data: WDSEventDB DOI 10.5281/zenodo.17547955, MD5 4ac57517151a5958ebc2226954254f8d shown on repository. License not resolved in extracted page; do not redistribute without verifying rights.

candidates.title: Materials experiment selection and shared formulation campaign
candidates.beneficiary: Small laboratories or formulation companies with expensive measurements.
candidates.outcome: Choose a measurement campaign that creates useful property coverage and deliverable formulations.
candidates.existing: NIST ThermoPlan/TDE directly supply experiment planning and coverage evaluation; NIST AFL already links AI-driven planning to robotic multimodal measurement in closed loop; scientific-value-function research formalizes experiment utility.
candidates.gap: No distinct gap established within this budget. Cross-party funding or application-specific acceptance could be useful, but not evidence of a new scientific capability.
candidates.disposition: Reject as current flagship: supplied solutions and physical validation requirements dominate. Preserve as candidate-selection evidence.
candidates.first_test: A buyer-specific documented unmet requirement and public measurement dataset would be necessary before a new experiment. Do not simulate generic Bayesian optimization and call it discovery.
candidates.falsifier: Already met by available TDE/AFL tooling at adequate scope/cost.
candidates.arrangement: Shared measurement campaigns remain hypothetical and would need real compatible interests.
